title: Knowing all letters
keyIdea: The alphabet has 26 letters. Each letter has a name, like bee for b, and two shapes: a capital and a small letter. Capital G and small g are one letter with one name. The letters come in a set order, from A to Z. Some letters are the same shape turned around, like b and d, so which way a letter faces matters. We use letter names to spell, for example cat is see, ay, tee.

kid: Every letter has a name. This is b. Its name is bee. We sing the names in the ABC song. Each letter has two shapes. A big one is a capital. A small one is for most words. G and g are the same letter.
Look at b and d. Turn b around and it is d! So check which way it faces. b has the stick first. d has its tummy first.
The letters go in order, A to Z. Sing it slowly: l, m, n, o, p. That is five letters, not one long word.
A letter has a name and a sound. c is called see. In cat it says k. To spell cat, say the names: see, ay, tee.
adult: This is alphabet knowledge, one of the strongest early predictors of learning to read. US Common Core RF.K.1.d asks children to recognise and name all upper- and lowercase letters. The English national curriculum for Year 1 asks pupils to name the letters of the alphabet in order and to use letter names to tell apart alternative spellings of the same sound.

Keep three ideas apart. The letter name is fixed (aitch for h). The letter sound, or phoneme, is what the letter usually says in a word (h as in hat). Phonics lessons teach the sounds first for reading, so children often know sounds before names. Both are needed: names stay the same while one sound can have several spellings, so names let you talk about spelling, for example k or c.

Common mistakes: reversing b, d, p and q, because in everyday life an object turned around is still the same object (mirror generalisation); hearing l-m-n-o-p in the song as one letter, elemeno; thinking a capital and its lowercase letter are two different letters, especially pairs that look different such as A and a, G and g, R and r; and giving the sound when asked for the name.

In the lab your child drags small letters to their capital partners, finds b, d, p and q, fills gaps in an alphabet train, picks a letter's name over its sound, and spells cat, kid and dog with letter names. Be careful to say names and sounds clearly and not to mix them in one sentence.

familyTip: Play I spy with letter names on signs and cereal boxes: 'I spy a capital M, em.' Then ask your child to find its small partner, m, somewhere else on the box.

visual.caption: Which capital is each small letter's partner? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: match small letters to capitals, find b, d, p and q, fill the alphabet train, tell names from sounds, and spell with letter names.

practice.prompt: Which small letter is the partner of capital G?
practice.hint: Say the name of capital G. Which small letter has the same name, gee?
practice.explain: G and g are one letter called gee. q has a tail too, but its name is cue.

practice.prompt: The alphabet has 26 letters. Mia can name {n} of them. How many more letters does she need to learn?
practice.hint: Start at {n} and count on to 26, or take {n} away from 26.
practice.explain: 26 take away {n} is {=26-n}, so Mia has {=26-n} more letters to learn.

practice.prompt: Which letter comes just after K in the alphabet?
practice.hint: Sing the ABC from H: h, i, j, k, ...
practice.explain: The order is j, k, l, m, so L comes just after K. J comes before it.

practice.prompt: Each letter has a capital and a small shape. How many shapes do {n} letters have?
practice.hint: Each letter gives two shapes. Count two for every letter.
practice.explain: Two shapes for each of {n} letters makes {=2*n} shapes, but still only {n} letter names.

pool.prompt: What is the name of the letter h?
pool.hint: Think of the ABC song, not the sound at the start of hat.
pool.explain: The name of h is aitch. huh is the sound it makes in hat, and ay is the name of a.

pool.prompt: Turn the letter d around, like in a mirror. Which letter do you get?
pool.hint: d has its tummy first. Where is the tummy after the flip?
pool.explain: After the flip the stick comes first and the tummy after it, so d turns into b.

pool.prompt: A word has {n} letters. To spell it out loud you say one letter name for each letter. How many names do you say?
pool.hint: One letter, one name. Count the letters.
pool.explain: {n} letters means you say {n} letter names, one for each letter.

pool.prompt: Sam sings l-m-n-o-p as one word. How many letters is that really?
pool.hint: Say each one slowly and hold up a finger for each name.
pool.explain: l, m, n, o and p are five letters. The song goes fast, so they can sound like one word.

pool.prompt: Is it c or k at the start of the word cat?
pool.hint: c and k can both say k. Think of how cat is spelt: see, ay, ...
pool.explain: cat is spelt see, ay, tee. k can make the same sound, but cat always uses c.

pool.prompt: Ali can say the alphabet up to letter number {n}. Z is letter number 26. How many letters are left?
pool.hint: Count on from {n} to 26, one letter at a time.
pool.explain: From letter {n} to letter 26 there are 26 take away {n}, which is {=26-n} letters left.

pool.prompt: Which pair is a capital and small letter of the same letter?
pool.hint: Say the name of each shape. Do they match?
pool.explain: A and a are both called ay. B and d, and P and q, are different letters.

pool.prompt: Which letter comes just before S in the alphabet?
pool.hint: Sing the ABC from P: p, q, and stop before s.
pool.explain: The order is q, r, s, t, so R comes just before S. T comes after it.
